title: Perf canary (prod) MVP: service + baselines + dashboards + alerting (umbrella)
creator: Talia Benson
dependencies: PR redwood#19193 (runtime build + kernel version tags)
PR redwood#19203 (control-plane config for canary target models)
PR redwood-model-registry#18577 (model version exposed to telemetry)
description:
Objective
Ship a lightweight, always-on production performance canary that detects per-model p95 latency regressions and tokens/sec drops with low noise, and routes actionable alerts to runtime + SRE with clear attribution signals (kernel vs scheduler vs infra).

Why
We’ve repeatedly seen regressions slip through staging benchmarks and only show up under real batching/queueing behavior and real fleet variability. We want an always-on signal that catches tail-latency and throughput changes early (ideally during limited rollout windows) and provides enough context to reduce time-to-mitigation (rollback/feature flag/fleet change revert).

Scope (MVP)
- Perf-canary service running synthetic workloads (no customer prompts) against a curated model list (Phase 1: 2–3 models, 1 region).
- Emit per-model metrics:
  - End-to-end latency p50/p95/p99
  - Runtime-only latency (if available) + breakdown: prefill, decode, queueing time
  - Tokens/sec (throughput)
  - Batch size distribution
  - KV cache hit-rate (optional; include only if signal is stable + low cost)
- Baseline store + regression evaluator:
  - Baselines keyed by (model, model_version, runtime_build, hardware_sku) and optionally region.
  - Regression = percent deviation beyond threshold + minimum sample count + dampening window (anti-flap).
- Dashboards + alert rules:
  - Warning alerts to #eng-runtime, paging only after tuning + policy approval.
  - Alert payload includes baseline vs observed, confidence/min-samples status, and links to dashboard/runbook.
- Deployment:
  - Helm + terraform wiring, safe defaults, explicit fanout guardrails (prevent accidental “run everywhere”).
  - A “safe disable” switch for fast turn-off without impacting inference.

Non-goals (MVP)
- Shadowing customer traffic or capturing any customer prompt content.
- Coupling to quality eval regressions (Applied ML owns separate eval harness).
- Full multi-region coverage; we will expand after Phase 1 is stable.

Milestones / plan
1) Requirements & design alignment (done in parallel)
   - Metric definitions + label set + cardinality review
   - Baseline computation policy + alert thresholds policy
2) Implementation
   - Service skeleton + synthetic prompt generator + request loop
   - Runtime instrumentation for queueing time + kernel/runtime tags
   - Baseline fetch + regression evaluator
3) Observability
   - Grafana dashboards (per model) + queries validated
   - Warning alerts wired to incident-bot formatting
4) Controlled rollout
   - Phase 1: us-east, 2–3 models; warnings only for 1–2 weeks
   - Tune thresholds / reduce false positives
5) Paging + rollout gates (post-MVP but track readiness here)
   - Enable paging for “top models” once noise is acceptable
   - Integrate with release gates (separate PM umbrella)

Acceptance criteria
Functional
- Canary runs continuously in prod (Phase 1) and produces stable per-model metrics for latency + tokens/sec.
- Baselines are stored and versioned such that model rollouts / runtime releases do not cause baseline ambiguity.
- Regression evaluator correctly triggers warning-level alerts when synthetic regression is induced (controlled experiment).
- Alert payload includes:
  - model + model_version
  - runtime_build + kernel selection tag (if applicable)
  - hardware SKU + region
  - observed vs baseline values + percent delta
  - sample size + dampening state
  - dashboard link + runbook link
Operational
- Canary overhead stays within budget (<0.5% GPU capacity per region for covered models). Validate with QPS caps + scheduler impact.
- No customer data: prompts are synthetic; logs/metrics contain no prompt strings; redaction + assertions in service.
- Fanout guardrails: configuration changes are validated/audited; cannot accidentally enable “all models/all regions” from a single config push.
- On-call readiness:
  - Runbook exists and is reviewed by SRE
  - Incident-bot routing is validated (dedupe keys, correct channels)

Rollout plan (Phase 1 proposal)
- Region: us-east
- Models: select 2–3: (1) top model by usage, (2) long-context/high-risk model, (3) newly optimized kernel model (if available)
- Alerting: warnings only for first 7–14 days; paging after threshold calibration + policy sign-off

Open questions
- Baseline drift strategy: fixed per runtime build vs rolling baseline with guardrails. (See ADR; track follow-up items in ENG-4874/ENG-4882.)
- Region/SKU-specific thresholds: default off for MVP, but ensure config supports it without cardinality blowups.
- KV cache hit-rate: include only if we can guarantee consistent measurement across model families.

Links
- Design doc (Confluence): perf regression canary design
- Baselines/thresholds ADR (Confluence): baseline computation + anti-flap strategy
- Dashboard spec (Confluence): panels + links expectations
- SRE policy (Confluence): per-model latency SLO mapping + paging rules
- Runbook (Confluence): perf regression canary alert triage

Notes
This is an umbrella ticket. Please track implementation work in sub-issues and link PRs as they land. We should treat Phase 1 stability (low noise, actionable attribution) as the gate to expand model coverage/top-10.
